product_one_liner.value: DataGrail automates data discovery and mapping, data-subject requests, consent management, and privacy-risk assessments for midmarket and enterprise brands.
product_one_liner.notes: The documentation describes the platform’s four privacy functions—discovery and mapping, DSR management, consent, and risk assessment—while the company press page identifies its audience as midmarket and enterprise customers.

pricing_page.notes: The official homepage navigation and company/footer links show product, solutions, resources, company, demo, and contact links, but no pricing link. This supports no public company pricing page.

named_customers.notes: named_customers: DataGrail’s customer case-study pages identify nCino as a user and feature Life360 as a customer. | named_customers.0: The nCino case-study page identifies nCino as a DataGrail user. | named_customers.1: The Life360 customer page identifies Life360 as a DataGrail customer.

employee_band.notes: The LinkedIn company profile reports 73 employees, which falls in the 51-100 band.

hq_location.notes: hq_city: The company press page states that DataGrail is headquartered in San Francisco, California. | hq_country: The company press page identifies its headquarters as San Francisco, California, which is in the United States.

founded_year.notes: The company’s press page quotes a report that says DataGrail was founded in May 2018, establishing the founding year.

eng_blog.notes: The Engineering-tagged Engineering Way article discusses engineering infrastructure and practices and is by Ignacio Zendejas, whom DataGrail identifies as its technical lead responsible for product architecture and development. A second Engineering-tagged post by Charlie Thomas explains design and implementation choices for the APIs used in DataGrail integrations; his profile identifies him as a DataGrail software engineer. Together these support at least two technical engineering posts.

public_docs.notes: The company homepage links to Documentation; its documentation home describes platform/product documentation, and the public API reference is another substantive article in the docs portal.

ai_ml_roles_open.notes: The live Greenhouse board lists three current roles—Senior Customer Success Manager, IT & Business Systems Manager, and Senior Demand Generation Manager—and none has an AI, ML, data-science, or related title.

model_provider.value: Claude Sonnet 5, hosted on AWS Bedrock
model_provider.notes: DataGrail’s Vera privacy-and-security documentation names Claude Sonnet 5 as the model and says it is hosted in AWS Bedrock.

compliance_certs.notes: compliance_certs: DataGrail’s security-focused page explicitly says it is HIPAA compliant and has SOC 2 Type II certification. Those are the two requested categories it names; Privacy Shield is outside the requested list. | compliance_certs.0: The security-focused page explicitly says DataGrail is HIPAA compliant. | compliance_certs.1: The security-focused page explicitly names SOC 2 Type II.

last_funding.notes: funding_stage: The fundraising profile labels the latest round Series C. | funding_date: The funding-history table identifies the latest Series C date as October 2022, represented as 2022-10. | funding_amount_usd: The fundraising profile identifies the latest deal as a $45 million Series C and lists October 2022 as its date.

raised_18mo.notes: The fundraising history identifies October 2022 as the latest round, well before the 18-month window beginning May 2025.

hiring_sdr_ae.notes: The Enterprise Account Executive and Mid Market Account Executive Greenhouse postings each show an Apply link and an application form. Although the board index does not list them, the individual live postings support hiring AEs.

launched_6mo.notes: DataGrail’s June 23, 2026 announcement introduces automated DROP compliance, a major product offering. June 2026 is within the six months before November 9, 2026.

leadership_change_12mo.notes: A profile records Christopher Wright as DataGrail’s VP of GTM Ops, Growth & AI beginning June 2026, inside the 12-month window. Separately, an executive-movement report says Amy Reagan Hollo was promoted from VP Operations to COO in May 2026. This supports a leadership change during the period.

crm_stack_signal.notes: crm_stack_signal: Current DataGrail job postings name Salesforce and Gong in the GTM stack, and the demand-generation role names HubSpot, Salesforce, Google Ads, LinkedIn Campaign Manager, and YouTube. These postings provide visible CRM and marketing-stack signals; Gong appears as a familiarity requirement, so the evidence is a signal rather than independent proof of deployment. | crm_stack_signal.0: The demand-generation posting names Salesforce and its sync with HubSpot. | crm_stack_signal.1: The enterprise AE posting names Gong as part of a modern GTM technology stack. | crm_stack_signal.2: The demand-generation posting describes HubSpot ownership and administration. | crm_stack_signal.3: The posting names Google Ads for paid-media campaigns. | crm_stack_signal.4: The posting names LinkedIn Campaign Manager for paid-media campaigns. | crm_stack_signal.5: The posting names YouTube as a paid-media campaign channel.
